subject: Request: Attribution & evidence for WAN-induced latency spikes on Private deployment
messages:
From: Daniel Morris <daniel.morris@vanguardhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, support@redwood.com
Cc: netops@vanguardhealth.com
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Observed token-level latency spikes during our colo provider maintenance

Hi Sean / Redwood team,

We started seeing 400–700ms tail spikes on model responses from our private deployment yesterday morning that line up with a scheduled maintenance window at our colo provider (transit provider performed a firmware update). The app logs show token delays that look network-bound rather than compute-bound.

Can Redwood confirm whether these events are attributable to customer-controlled networking (WAN/transit) versus an infrastructure issue inside the private runtime? Vanguard needs a formal attribution for our compliance audit and to decide if an SLA exception applies.

I attached a pcap of RTTs and a short timeline from our edge router. Happy to set up a joint troubleshooting call.

Thanks,
Daniel Morris
Sr. Cloud Ops Engineer | Vanguard Health
[Attachment: vanguard-wan-trace-2026-12-09.pcap (pcap)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Morris <daniel.morris@vanguardhealth.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, support@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Observed token-level latency spikes during our colo provider maintenance

Thanks Daniel — appreciate the packet capture and timeline.

Short answer: based on what you shared it looks like network egress/jitter in your colo/transit path, but we need a couple of artifacts from our side to make a formal attribution and sign off on any SLA exception. Specifically we need:

- Redwood-side request/response timing for the window you shared (per-connection token timings and the runtime trace).
- The private runtime host kernel logs around the event (we'll pull these).
- A short mutual action plan (MAP) documenting the outage window and the parties responsible for mitigation steps — this makes any carveout auditable.

I will pull the runtime traces and prod logs and loop back by EOD tomorrow. Can you confirm the exact maintenance window (start/end timestamps) and whether any local NAT/edge changes were applied? Also: is Vanguard ok with Redwood uploading runtime evidence to the Drive link you provided, or would you prefer a secure transfer (SFTP/ShareFile)?

Proposing a quick 30-min joint call tomorrow 10:00am ET to walk traces if that works.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Dec 9, 2026 at 11:03 AM Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Daniel — appreciate the packet capture and timeline.

Hi all — copying the proposed evidence and attribution checklist we use for Private/VPC SLA exceptions so we're consistent:

1) Customer evidence: edge pcap, edge router/gateway logs, maintenance ticket IDs from the colo/transit provider, and exact maintenance timestamps. (Daniel: you already sent the pcap; please add provider ticket IDs if you can.)
2) Redwood evidence: per-request token timing (ingest->first-token, per-token delta), runtime host NIC statistics, kernel drops if any, and application-level retries.
3) Correlation: we need an aligned timeline (UTC) that overlays your pcap and our token logs so the adjudication team can see if spikes precede or follow internal processing queues.
4) Proposed SLA outcome: if correlation shows network egress/jitter originating inside client-controlled edge or transit, we propose treating event as customer-controlled (no uptime credit). If evidence shows queuing or degraded throughput inside the private runtime (e.g., kernel NIC queue growth, device interrupts), we propose Redwood-owned incident and standard SLA remediation.

We can prepare a draft MAP and upload to the Drive folder (I will put a template under the MAP folder). I'll also attach the runtime logs once Sean pulls them.

If Vanguard wants legal/procurement involved early (for a temporary exception amendment), call that out and we will loop them in.

Best,
Irene Choi
Product Operations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mutual-action-plan-vanguard.docx]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Daniel Morris <daniel.morris@vanguardhealth.com>
Cc: legal@redwood.com, procurement@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Observed token-level latency spikes during our colo provider maintenance

Hi Daniel — quick update from the runtime side after correlating your pcap with our logs for 2026-12-09 02:00:00–02:45:00 UTC:

- Redwood runtime shows flat CPU/GPU utilization and normal scheduling; we do not see token-processing queue growth.
- Per-request timing indicates elevated inter-packet latency between the customer edge and the runtime (consistent with the RTT variance in your pcap).
- Host NIC stats show increased retransmits on the egress interface, timed to the maintenance window.

Based on this correlation, the evidence points to customer/transit-controlled network jitter as the proximate cause. Per our shared-responsibility SLA language, we'd classify this as customer-controlled infrastructure for attribution purposes.

Next steps we propose:
- Finalize a short MAP (Irene will upload a draft).
- Vanguard to confirm whether you'd like Redwood to treat this as an SLA exception (formal note on the account) or simply an investigation note for your audit. If you request an exception, procurement/legal will need the MAP + evidence bundle (we've uploaded our runtime logs to the Drive link).

Cc'ing legal and procurement so they can prepare the exception amendment template (if needed).

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Director, Site Reliability | Redwood Inference
